facts.claim: Battery bus voltage dropped to 23.8 V at 14:31:42 UTC, below nominal 24.5 V minimum threshold.
Communications transmitter RF power output decreased by 4.2 dBm following EPS bus voltage drop.

inferences.claim: Power instability in EPS main bus is the primary driver of communication signal degradation.

recommendations.action: Execute COMMS-04 procedure Step 1: Verify battery bus voltage and switch high-power payloads to standby.

T-19281.content: EPS Battery Bus Voltage measured 23.8V (Warning threshold 24.5V).

T-19282.content: S-Band Transceiver signal level dropped to -102.4 dBm due to bus power throttle.

INC-047.content: Historical incident: EPS voltage drop caused automatic comms transmitter power backoff. Resolved by executing COMMS-04 payload load shedding.

COMMS-04.content: COMMS-04: Communications Degradation Procedure. Step 1: Check battery bus voltage. Step 2: Verify comms current draw. Step 3: Shed secondary thermal heaters.
